## 2. How to draw the wireframe so it is read correctly

You can use any tool that exports SVG (Figma, Inkscape, Illustrator, Penpot, or plain text editing).

- **Page size:** use `viewBox="0 0 210 297"` (A4 in millimetres). If your canvas is another size, keep the A4 proportion.
- **Fields:** write the field name in curly braces where the text goes, for example `{course.code}` or `{assignment.title}`.
  Plain words also work ("Course title"), but braces are unambiguous. The full list of field names is in section 5.
- **The logo:** draw a dashed rectangle and write `{logo}` inside it. Its **height** sets the logo's size at 100%.
  Its left/centre/right position is only a default: the person using the app chooses the real position.
- **Group members:** write `{group.members}` once, on a block that shows one or two sample rows, to show how a row looks.
- **Fixed words** such as "Submitted to:" are copied exactly as written.
- **Lines and boxes:** draw them as lines/rectangles. Stroke width and colour are respected.
- **Instructions vs content:** text in `<desc>`, `<title>`, in small grey notes, and sentences like "group mode: list
  {group.members} here" are **instructions to the AI**, never printed on the cover. Only `{fields}` and plain words
  you draw as page text become content.
- **Type:** add a small note next to a text item if you care, for example `20px bold uppercase serif`.
  Notes belong in a clearly separate corner or in a `<desc>` element; they are instructions, not page content.
- **Margins:** the wireframe's outer margin is ignored, because the app lets the user change margins. Draw your
  content inside the area you want and the AI will lay it out relative to that area.
- **Individual vs group:** if you only draw one, the AI designs the other in the same style and says so in its notes.

## 3. The task (AI: read from here)

You are adding a template to **GetCovered**, a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript web app that creates A4 cover pages for
university assignments. Read the attached **SVG wireframe** and produce a template that looks like it.

A template is exactly two files. The app supplies everything else (editor, A4 page, margins, alignment, logo size and
position, printing, saving). A template only decides **how the fields are arranged and styled**.

### What you must output, in this order, with nothing before it

1. `assets/js/templates/<id>.js` in one complete code block.
2. `assets/css/templates/<id>.css` in one complete code block.
3. The exact edit for `assets/js/templates/registry.js` (an `import` line and the new `templates` array).
4. **Notes**: a short bullet list of (a) assumptions you made, (b) anything in the wireframe you could not
   reproduce and why, (c) any field you put in `ignores` and why (aim for none).

Do not ask questions. Do not explain the code. Do not output anything else. (If the person's message tells you to
write the files to disk or to reply differently, follow the person's message; the output *content* is the same.)

## 4. Hard rules (a template that breaks any of these fails the project's tests)

**Every field is shown.** Every field in the "must render" table in section 5 has to appear on the page, in **both**
individual and group mode, by reading it through `ctx`. If the wireframe has no place for a field, find a sensible
place in the same visual style and list it under Notes. Only if it truly cannot fit, list it in `ignores` with a reason
of at least a full sentence. Never drop a field silently.

**Read data only through `ctx`:**

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `ctx.f('course.code')` | Safe markup for one field. Shows lorem ipsum while empty, so previews are never blank. |
| `ctx.has('individual.extra')` | `true` only when the person filled it in. Use it for optional text so nothing shows when empty. |
| `ctx.members()` | Group rows as `[{ name, id, hasName, hasId }]`, empty rows already removed. Render `name`/`id` only when `hasName`/`hasId`. |
| `ctx.logo()` | The logo block, already sized and aligned. **The only way to place the logo.** |
| `ctx.mode` | `'individual'` or `'group'`. Branch the layout on it. |

`html` escapes every plain string for you (for example `m.name`), and arrays of `html\`\`` results (from `.map()`) can be
interpolated directly. `submission.mode` counts as handled as soon as you read `ctx.mode` to branch the layout.

A wrong field path throws an error that lists the right ones.

What `ctx.f()` gives you: **inline markup** (plain escaped text, with `<br>` between lines for multi-line fields).
It is never uppercased or otherwise transformed, so use CSS `text-transform` for that. While a field is empty it is
`<span class="gc-dummy">lorem ipsum</span>`, which is safe to nest inside any element of yours.

What `ctx.logo()` gives you: `<div class="gc-logo">` containing the image. That div is `display:flex; width:100%` and
the app aligns the image inside it left, centre or right according to the user's **Logo position** setting.
**So the element that wraps `ctx.logo()` must be as wide as the row it sits in** (its own full-width row, or a flex
child with `flex: 1`). If you wrap it in a shrink-to-fit box (`flex: none`, `width: auto`, `inline-block`), the Logo
position setting silently stops working. Never set `max-width` on it either.
When the wireframe puts the logo **beside** other content (a banner, a name next to it), the recommended pattern is a
flex row where the logo's wrapper has `flex: 1` and the other item takes the rest (for example `flex: 2`), or, if
the layout allows, give the logo its own full-width row. Say in Notes which you chose. The logo may sit on a dark
colour, but it is the person's own image, so do not tint or filter it.

**Markup safety.** `render(ctx)` returns the result of the `html` tag imported from `'../core/html.js'`. Put values inside
`${...}` only. Never build HTML with string concatenation, `innerHTML`, or `raw()`. Typed text must never become markup.

**CSS scoping.** Every selector must start with `.gc-page[data-template="<id>"]`, including selectors inside `@media`.
A selector without that prefix fails the tests.

**Alignment.** Use `var(--gc-align)` for `text-align` and `var(--gc-justify)` for flex `justify-content`/`align-items`
on the parts that should follow the user's "Content alignment" setting (normally the heading block and the date).
The CSS file must contain at least one of them. Note the app's default Content alignment is **centre**. If the wireframe
is clearly left- or right-aligned, still use the variables (so the setting works), and in Notes tell the person which
Content alignment to choose to match the wireframe (for example "Set Content alignment to Left").

**The logo.** Set `--gc-logo-base` on the template root to the logo height at 100% size, in px (take it from the
dashed `{logo}` rectangle: 1 mm = 3.7795 px). Never set a `width` or `height` on the logo or its image.

**Layout.** The page is an A4 flex column (`display:flex; flex-direction:column`) with the user's margins already applied
as padding. Build inside it with flex or grid. Use `flex: 1` and `margin-top: auto` to push blocks down.
Do not set the page's size, padding, margins, background, or overflow.

**Nothing else.** No `<script>`, `<style>`, `@import`, `@font-face`, external URLs, web fonts, or new image files.
Inline `style=""` attributes are not allowed. Use font stacks that already exist on every computer, or inherit.
The default font is `inherit` (Book Antiqua, with a bundled lookalike); keep it unless the wireframe clearly asks otherwise.
Small decorations in pure CSS (borders, rules, background colours, grey boxes on inner elements) are fine.
The app already forces backgrounds to print, so do not add `print-color-adjust`. Comments in your files are welcome.
Fixed English words ("Section", "Submitted to") are fine. You may add a short label such as "Group" for a field the
wireframe leaves unlabelled.

**Robust layout.** Text must wrap: use `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on user text. Never give text boxes a
fixed height. Cover pages are one A4 page, so keep content compact enough that long titles and 12 group members still fit.

## 6. How to translate the wireframe

1. **Content box.** At the default 1-inch margins the writable area is **159.2 mm × 246.2 mm (601.7 px × 930.5 px)**.
   Treat the area inside the wireframe's outer margin as that content box. Express positions **relative to it**
   (flex, grid, percentages, `margin-top: auto`), never as absolute offsets from the page edge, because the user can
   change the margins and alignment.
2. **Sizes.** Convert millimetres to px (×3.7795). A font size in the wireframe's notes can be used as written.
   If a size is not given, estimate it from the text's height in the SVG (a capital letter is about 70% of the font size).
3. **Spacing.** Reproduce vertical rhythm: small gaps become fixed `margin`/`gap` values; one large empty stretch
   becomes `flex: 1` or `margin-top: auto` so the bottom block stays at the bottom for any content length.
4. **Columns and tables.** Side-by-side blocks become `display:flex` with `min-width:0` children (so long words wrap), or
   a `table`/grid when columns must line up. A vertical rule between columns is a bordered element or a thin `div`.
5. **Mapping.** `{field}` placeholders map directly. Plain words map by meaning using the table in section 5.
   Fixed words stay as literal text.
6. **Group mode.** `ctx.members()` returns a list: render one row (or one name line and one ID line) per member and
   let the column grow downward. If the wireframe shows only individual mode, design group mode in the same style.
7. **Optional text.** `individual.extra` appears only when `ctx.has('individual.extra')` is true.
8. **Size budget.** Design for the worst case: a 3-line title and 12 group members must still fit the content box
   (246.2 mm / 930 px tall at default margins), so use flexible spacing with a small minimum, not big fixed gaps, and let
   group members use a compact list or two columns if needed.
9. **Lorem ipsum lines.** Empty fields show greyed lorem ipsum in the preview (class `gc-dummy`) and the app hides it
   when printing. A line that would otherwise be empty when printed can be hidden like this:
   `.gc-page[data-template="<id>"] .row:has(> .gc-dummy:only-child) { display: none }` inside `@media print`.
   Adding this to your line elements is recommended, as Classic does.

## 7. Check your work before you answer

Silently verify each item, and fix anything that fails:

- [ ] Every field in section 5's first table is read with `ctx` in **both** modes, and is visibly placed.
- [ ] `id` is lowercase letters/digits/dashes and **identical** in the JS file, the CSS selectors, the file names,
      and the registry import.
- [ ] `css` points to `assets/css/templates/<id>.css`. `version: 1`. `name` and `description` are set.
- [ ] `render(ctx)` returns `html\`...\`` and interpolates only `ctx` values or nested `html\`\``.
- [ ] Every CSS selector starts with `.gc-page[data-template="<id>"]` (also inside `@media`).
- [ ] The CSS uses `var(--gc-align)` and/or `var(--gc-justify)`, and sets `--gc-logo-base`.
- [ ] The logo comes only from `ctx.logo()`, nothing sets its width or height, and its wrapper spans the full row
      width (so Logo position works).
- [ ] No scripts, styles, imports, fonts, URLs, or inline `style` attributes.
- [ ] The layout still works with a 3-line title, a very long word, an empty optional field, and 12 members.
- [ ] If the wireframe is not centre-aligned, Notes says which Content alignment to choose.
- [ ] You output exactly: the JS file, the CSS file, the registry edit, then Notes. Nothing else.
